Happy Wednesday! It's **Swin**. Election Day in the United States is less than
a month away. If the public polls (as well as the private _Republican_ polls)
are right, it looks like we're headed for an electoral slaughterhouse for the
GOP and Team Trump.

Last week, '**First Draft** ' brought you news on how Republican consultants
and pollsters are waking up to the idea that their party's big, anti-**Hasan
Piker** midterm strategy [is one giant, very expensive
failure](https://zeteo.com/p/top-republicans-privately-admit-their). In
today's '**First Draft** ,' we'll fill you in on yet another dose of
pre-2026-elections panic emanating from the elite ranks of **Donald Trump** 's
Republican Party - and boy, is this one a doozy.

"**Fuck a duck** ," one close Trump adviser told me this month. "**It 's
looking bad**."

That's how one source summed up the mood coming from so, so, so many national
and state Republican Party officials, political operatives, GOP candidates,
and Trumpland bigwigs.

[Subscribe now](https://zeteo.com/subscribe)

Standard caveat: Who knows what will happen in November, but for now, what
you're hearing isn't liberal wishcasting. The pervasive and deepening freakout
on the American right is extremely real, in part because their own internal
[polling](https://zeteo.com/p/top-republicans-privately-admit-their) is
_telling them to be afraid_ of losing the House and quite possibly the Senate
too. And it's largely due to the [gross unpopularity of
their](https://zeteo.com/p/trump-advisers-worry-he-could-sink) infallible god-
king, President Donald Trump.

But this adviser wasn't just talking about the overall doom and gloom within
their party. They were specifically bemoaning the distinct possibility that
their side's election-corrupting schemes are going to fail this time around.

All the Republican Party wanted to do this year was rig the midterm elections
after Trump told them to launch a mid-decade gerrymandering war, then walk
away scot-free with some extra wins under their belt. Turns out, life may have
other plans for them. Several prominent GOP operatives and Trump advisers I've
spoken to lately point to their side's own private polling, as well as public
data and sentiment, that indicate that Republicans in Texas may have (in
common political parlance) **" dummymandered"** themselves into some
Democratic congressional wins this cycle. The primary reason this could
conceivably (maybe even _likely_) occur is because conservatives, acting under
President Trump's explicit call to action, redrew the Texas congressional map
in ways meant to lock in Trump's significant gains with Latino voters in 2024.
But the weight of Trump's malaise-filled economy - as well as his party's
dedication to [attacking and kidnapping](https://zeteo.com/p/trumps-violent-
crackdowns-on-us-cities) as many Hispanic Texan voters' friends and family as
possible - has greatly eroded those gains, and leaves many of those voters in
redrawn districts [swinging towards the
Dems](https://www.reuters.com/world/us/republicans-may-have-gerrymandered-
their-way-into-texas-sized-latino-problem-2026-09-23/).

Who could have foreseen that intentionally making a crucial voting bloc poorer
and less safe would cause those voters to get mad?

But it's not just Texas.
